english_translation: One follows being. Truth is third, because after something is in itself, it must be seen whether it be like the exemplar according to which it was formed. If the thing is similar, it follows that it turns itself through goodness toward its exemplar as to the like and similar.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico elaborates the order of transcendental properties—being → one → true → good—as a graduated scale of metaphysical perfection. [INFERRED] Each property depends on prior ones: a thing must *be* to possess unity; must be unified to conform to its exemplar (truth); must truly conform to possess ordered orientation toward its source (goodness). This order applies to all creation but angels exemplify it most perfectly.

The philosophical function is to transform the angelic hierarchy into a metaphysical scale: not merely nine orders but nine degrees of realized perfection. The seraph, as highest, maximally participates in all transcendental properties—maximum being (not quasi-non-being like matter), perfect unity (intellect and will undivided), complete truth (total conformity to divine exemplar), perfect goodness (pure charity and orientation toward God). Lower angels participate proportionally, their perfection decreasing by degree. [VERIFIED] This grades the hierarchy: each angel is measured by how fully it actualizes the transcendental properties.

[VERIFIED] Heptaplus develops this through the layers: each layer reveals transcendental perfection at a different interpretive depth. Commento emphasizes the seraph as unity exemplified in love. Oration describes human ascent as progressive actualization of these properties. Being & Unity grounds it: the transcendental order measures all participated being.
metaphysical_theme: Transcendental hierarchy (being → one → true → good) mirrored in the angelic hierarchy; the seraph as exemplar of created unity, possessing maximum participation in the transcendental properties

notes: HARVESTER passage U.3.2 introduces the seraph as the exemplar of transcendental perfection. This is crucial: the seraph is not merely the first of the nine orders but the creature that most completely realizes the metaphysical properties (being, one, true, good) that characterize all creation. In Commento and Oration, the seraph becomes the model for human virtue—humans aspire to seraphic unity and love precisely because the seraph embodies the transcendental order perfected.
